# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🖐 ✌ ✌ 🤟 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤝]

I can see a green light, display `0`, and a large button labelled “PUSH TO DEFUSE.” The wires are, from top to bottom, green, yellow, red. I cannot interpret the gestures’ meaning, so I will report the bomb state plainly to both teammates and tell Blind not to act until the manual’s instructions are known.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 0, green light, and a large button marked PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires top to bottom: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 red. Please provide the manual instruction.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb state: display 0, green light, large button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires top to bottom are green, yellow, red. Do not act until Mute gives the manual instruction.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ☝ 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute has sent three gestures: an OK-hand sign, an index finger pointing up, and a thumbs-down sign. Blind has sent a thumbs-up sign, which I cannot treat as confirmation of a safe action. I will relay the exact observed signals and ask Mute to provide an unambiguous instruction before Blind touches anything.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute just signalled: OK-hand, index finger up, thumbs down. I do not know the gesture code; do not act yet. Your thumbs-up was seen.")
speak(to="mute", text="Please give Blind an unambiguous manual instruction using a defined gesture code, or signal clearly which wire or button action is required. Bomb remains display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires green yellow red.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The display and controls are still unchanged. Mute’s single ☝ may indicate wire 1, but the meaning is not established; Blind has made the same gesture, which is also ambiguous. I will establish a simple code rather than risk an action: Mute should identify the required control and action explicitly through gestures, while Blind waits.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please use this code from now on: gesture ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, 🤟 for wire 3. Then gesture 👍 for press, 👎 for do not press, and ✋ for cut. Send the control gesture and action gesture in that order.")
speak(to="blind", text="Bomb remains display 0, green light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires green yellow red. Mute has not given a confirmed instruction. Do not touch anything yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵]

The bomb is unchanged. Mute again signalled ☝, which under the code I proposed means wire 1, but no action instruction has been supplied. Blind signalled 🫵, apparently addressing me, but I cannot infer a safe operation from it. I will ask Mute to provide the action gesture and tell Blind that wire 1 is only a tentative identification, not permission to act.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute again signalled the code for wire 1, but has not signalled cut or press. Do not act yet. Please signal whether you need me to relay anything.")
speak(to="mute", text="I received wire 1. Now send exactly one action gesture: 👍 means press button, ✋ means cut wire, 👎 means do not act. Then I will relay it to Blind.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
BUTTON [large] [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵]

Mute has now sent ✋, which matches the action code I established for “cut.” Combined with the earlier ☝ identifying wire 1, this is an instruction to cut the green first wire. I will relay that exact instruction to Blind; I will not claim it has been carried out.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Instruction from Mute: cut wire 1, the green wire. Do it now.")
wait()
```
